title: [review] project-LICHEN-2auf.44.7.1: Unbounded HashMap growth in AnnounceState last_relay_map
description:
## Problem

`AnnounceState::last_relay_map` (`HashMap<[u8; 8], u16>`) grows without bound. Every new originator IID seen causes an insertion with no eviction. There is no time-based expiration, no capacity limit, and no pruning.

In a production mesh with hundreds of nodes, each sending periodic announcements, the map will grow to the number of distinct originators seen over the lifetime of the process.

## Risk

- **DoS vector**: An attacker flooding unique forged IIDs can exhaust memory
- **Stale suppression**: A node that goes offline and restarts with a wrapped sequence may be permanently suppressed because its stale entry never expires
- **Silent resource leak**: On memory-constrained devices (replaying with the std-simulator), this causes OOM without obvious cause

## Evidence

The `should_relay` method inserts with no bound check:
```rust
self.last_relay_map.insert(*originator_iid, seq_num);
```

No eviction path exists in `AnnounceState`. The `Default` impl provides an empty map, and the only mutation path is `should_relay` which only inserts.

## Fix

Add an entry cap (e.g. 256 originators) with LRU eviction, or add time-based expiration requiring a clock parameter. For no_std compatibility (if this moves out of std-gated code later), a fixed-size array or `heapless::LinearMap` would be preferable.
